findings.reason: §10 is the plan's only live-fleet measure and its own wording gates on every other section, so the declared waits must include s59 or the measurement can run against a fleet that has not taken the last landing change.
findings.text: `plan-section-depends-on` lists §10's waits through s58 and omits s59, while §59 changes what a landing arm submits (its profile options) and §10's deliverable is "a measurement over 24 hours of the live fleet after the other sections have landed"; a §10 dispatch on the declared graph is released before s59 lands, exactly the case already answered for s51–s58

findings.reason: the followup is the dispatch chain, so an enumeration that omits s59 leaves a declared implementable section unqueued and the plan reading complete while work remains; this is the defect the author already answered twice for earlier sections.
findings.text: the open followup `f-dwl-s50` enumerates "sections 51, 53, 55, 56, 57 and 58" as the remaining work while `plan-section-declarations` now records s59 implementable, so the chain a coordinator follows stops one section short of the plan's own remaining work (and the same followup's prompt still names `§49`, which its body does not close)

findings.reason: a worker taking the sentence at its word may add the profile's `--mem`/`--cpus-per-task` beside the hardcoded ones, producing a submission with duplicated scheduler flags, where the accurate statement ("the values are fixed, and reservation and gres are absent") directs it to replace them.
findings.text: §59 states that "Neither adds the submission options an H200 arm needs: … an explicit `--mem` … `--cpus-per-task=..., … a `--time`", but both changed paths already emit them: `landing_measure.py:1084-1086` passes `--cpus-per-task={POPULATION_WORKERS}`, `--mem=32G` and `--time={bound}` in every landing-arm `sbatch` argv, so the return value carries no fixed option set: the defect is that the values are hardcoded per call site rather than declarable, and that no reservation or gres is passed at all

findings.reason: the optional/mandatory split fixes the accepted config surface and the load-time validation the section's second done-when case measures, so the plan must say which fields are required (memory, at least, if the refusal stands).
findings.text: the deliverable says a profile carries "optionally a reservation, a gres request, a memory, a CPU count and a default time" and then says "A profile whose memory is 0 or absent is refused at load, naming the profile", so memory is described as optional and as mandatory in the same paragraph; a worker cannot tell whether `{partition: rigel}` alone is a valid profile or a load-time refusal

findings.reason: the negative control is the evidence that the case can fail, and a control that misdescribes the base it runs against will either fail for the wrong reason or be rewritten to the actual base, so the section should name the option set the base `sbatch` argv carries (partition, mem, cpus, time) and the one it lacks (reservation, gres).
findings.text: the negative control says that at base the first case fails "with the submission carrying the partition alone", but no changed submission path submits the partition alone: a landing arm's argv carries `--mem=32G`, `--cpus-per-task=…` and a `--time` beside it, and the declared-gate path records further fields, so a base-arm assertion written to match this sentence asserts something no base call produces

findings.reason: an unmeasured deliverable clause is a clause the gate cannot hold, and this one is what keeps the H200 arm's temp files off the shared filesystem.
findings.text: the deliverable requires that the submitted job "keeps `TMPDIR` node-local and runs the project's interpreter directly, without `uv`", and no case in the done-when measures either condition, so a node could satisfy every listed case while submitting a job that runs through `uv` or a non-node-local `TMPDIR`
